chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
And I asked him about two slave brothers, whether they should be separated, and about a woman and her child, so he said: 'No, it is forbidden (to separate them) unless they wish to do so.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to separate enslaved siblings or a mother and child in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Sama'a clarifies the default legal status of enslaved family units, establishing that separation is prohibited (haram) unless explicitly consented to by the individuals involved. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving familial bonds within the institution of slavery, treating the 'unless' clause as a condition of voluntary consent rather than arbitrary discretion.
